assessments.basis: The paper directly contrasts familiar named-game performance with freshly generated anonymous zero-sum matrices and reports 34%/18%/2% success on 2x2/3x3/5x5 anonymous games; three solved few-shot examples further reduce anonymous 2x2 success from 34% to 10%. Procedural generation removes exact-instance memorization and supports a semantic-lookup confound.
assessments.scope: Supports a memorization/template-matching confound in the paper's Qwen3.5-9B matrix-game setup. Named textbook games and random anonymous matrices are not a perfect same-matrix label-only intervention, so the full gap is not assigned solely to naming and is not generalized to all named benchmarks.

assessments.basis: On the same 50-game evaluation sets, the paper reports both oracle best-of-4 exploitability selection and pass@1: at 5x5 SFT is 0.61±0.09 versus 0.33±0.07 and VERGE is 0.37±0.22 versus 0.21±0.18. It also explicitly treats the Qwen3-32B 8%-valid strict-JSON result as a format-stress diagnostic rather than a pure reasoning score.
assessments.scope: Strong evidence that decoding/verification and serialization are part of the measured system for this benchmark. It does not make best-of-k illegitimate when multi-sample verified decoding is the deployed policy, and the 32B format-stress result is not a capacity estimate.

assessments.basis: VERGE 5x5 best-of-4 success varies 58%/40%/14% across three training seeds, and a larger 150-game replication reports VERGE 0.42±0.18 at 5x5 and 0.16±0.15 at 7x7 versus SFT 0.63±0.01 and 0.28±0.05. The paper explicitly limits the claim to high seed sensitivity rather than stable mean superiority.
assessments.scope: Supports seed-instability and checkpoint-selection risk for this VERGE recipe and payoff-game transfer setting; it does not show verifier rewards are ineffective or that all RLVR recipes have unstable seeds.

assessments.basis: TSCG-Agentic-Bench spans about 19,000 calls and 12 models. In the small-model catalog test, Mistral 7B changes from 35.0% natural accuracy to 80.0% conservative TSCG at 20 tools and 30.0% to 75.3% at 50; Gemma 3 4B changes from 24.3% to 87.5% at 50. Text-baseline decomposition shows several large JSON-baseline gains are primarily representation/format effects rather than compression, directly supporting protocol-sensitivity.
assessments.scope: Supports large schema-representation effects in the released TAB/TSCG conditions. It does not establish JSON as universally inferior, and raw evaluation logs are not fully public; frontier and well-adapted models show different response profiles.

assessments.basis: Within the same Qwen3 14B benchmark, natural accuracy is 90.2% at 20 tools, conservative TSCG reaches 99.3%, while balanced TSCG falls to 84.1%; across 10/20/50 tools balanced is below natural by 8.7/6.1/5.0 points, and parameter-F1 shows the same conservative-versus-balanced split.
assessments.scope: Strong evidence that one schema-transformation profile can invert by model/configuration and should be regression-tested per model/version. It does not establish conservative TSCG as universally optimal; other models benefit from balanced compression.

assessments.basis: The paper evaluates repeated monitoring on identical anchor streams over 60 seeds and two datasets. Naive rolling z-tests at fixed alpha false-alarm on 75% of HelpSteer2 and 67% of TL;DR no-drift streams, including 16/60 and 10/60 pre-change detections; the anchor e-process holds false-alarm near 0.03 and detects the tested real judge changes, with 60/60 correct version-bump attribution and 110/120 strict-prompt attribution at guard width 300.
assessments.scope: Strong evidence that uncorrected repeated fixed-alpha testing is unsafe for the paper's continuous judge-monitoring construction and that a fixed human anchor can separate tested judge drift from system drift. It does not imply every rolling monitor has the same false-alarm rate or that the featured anchor settings are globally optimal.

assessments.basis: The peer-reviewed Reasoning Web tutorial formally defines subset-minimal justifications, gives a complete Reiter hitting-set-tree enumeration algorithm, proves its completeness, and exhibits a linear-size EL knowledge-base family with exactly 2^n justifications. This is direct formal evidence for all-alternative-minimal-support enumeration and its worst-case exponential frontier.
assessments.scope: Direct precedent for decidable description-logic entailment oracles only. It is not Lean-specific and does not establish practical completeness, tractability or operational utility for unrestricted theorem-prover search.

assessments.basis: Bienvenu, Figueira and Lafourcade define weighted sums of minimal supports, prove every WSMS measure is equivalent to the Shapley value of a suitably defined cooperative game, and establish tractable data complexity for a broad query class including all unions of conjunctive queries, while ordinary query-answer Shapley is #P-hard even for simple conjunctive queries.
assessments.scope: Strong formal evidence that minimal-support families can underwrite tractable Shapley-equivalent responsibility in database-query settings. It does not establish that the same weights or tractability carry to Lean proof search, non-monotone bounded search utility, or persistent lemma admission.
